title: Defending New Orleans music as a complete style
summary: Answering criticism that New Orleans music disappoints, Colyer says it is a complete style he will keep playing and improving without moving on.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: uh well i want to go back perhaps just a bit before you came to the world um i think that one of the big criticisms been leveled against new orleans jess since the war it's been of people who've gone down there and perhaps been disappointed found that you know there's not the vitality they'd expected or something like that i mean i know you don't share that opinion but would you like to say anything about that say what had you had you had any misgivings before you got to new orleans about the music at all about its you know continuing value and so on no uh only with with people in england that

didn't share my views and i consider new orleans music is a complete style and will always remain so i see no reason at all i i naturally we we know that there aren't new orleans musicians carrying on the tradition which is tremendously unfortunate but we'll always play in that style or i shall and i shall always try and improve the band's performance but in a new orleans way not in any way the timbres or orders the essential style and the idiom i think that's good as it is you can always play in that idiom and enjoy it i never get frustrated or want to move on to anything else and i'm more concerned with carrying on what i think is a worthwhile tradition a worthwhile music somebody's going to carry it on somebody's got to yeah right well um many of your contemporaries
